name: Estonia
headline: FIND YOUR SPOT ON THE COAST OF *ESTONIA*
intro: Half the country is forest and the coast is 3,800km long once you count the islands. You will not have to share.

mustSee.name: Tallinn Old Town
mustSee.note: Small enough to walk in an afternoon, and worth doing before the cruise ships dock at nine.

mustSee.name: Saaremaa
mustSee.note: The big island. Windmills, juniper, and a meteorite crater in a farmer's field.

mustSee.name: Tartu
mustSee.note: University town, better food than Tallinn, half the price.

mustSee.name: Lahemaa National Park
mustSee.note: An hour from Tallinn. Bog boardwalks, manor houses and empty beaches.

seasons.spring: April is grey and thawing. May is the one — light until ten, birds back, nothing booked out yet.
seasons.summer: June and July barely get dark. Midsummer is the biggest night of the year and the whole country leaves the cities for it.
seasons.autumn: September for the colour in the bogs. October gets wet and the island ferries start cancelling in wind.
seasons.winter: Dark by four and properly cold. The sea freezes hard enough for ice roads to the islands some years, which is a genuinely strange drive.

transport: Buses beat trains for most routes and they're cheap and modern — Lux Express between the cities. Ferries to Saaremaa and Hiiumaa go from Virtsu and Rohuküla and take cars; book ahead in July. You want a car for the coast and the bogs, and nothing else.
